By the time the aquatic larva reaches metamorphic climax, the wet weight has increased substantially to 0.3 grams , representing more than a tenfold gain from the hatchling stage. The species exhibits a prolonged breeding season coinciding with the monsoon rains, during which gravid females produce multiple clutches. The species' ability to persist into advanced age is likely facilitated by its relatively low predation rate in arboreal microhabitats and its capacity to exploit a stable, year-round supply of invertebrate prey. Comparative analyses within the Rhacophoridae indicate that such extended lifespans are associated with moderate adult body size and delayed senescence, patterns that align with the broader pace-of-life continuum observed across tropical anurans.
